feature: Drag with a row picked moves the whole animation
summary: Pick a row under a clip by its name, then drag the layer on the canvas: every key of that row moves by the same amount (for Position, the whole path) instead of a new key landing at the playhead. The row's right-click Easing now offers the same curve list a segment does.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Open the sample recording, type a title over it, right-click the title's clip and choose Animate > Position, then at three seconds drag the title to the right so the path has two keys.

try.do: Put the playhead at two seconds, between the two Position keys.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the word Position on the row under the title's clip to pick the row.
Drag the title down on the canvas and let go.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Scrub from one second to three: the whole move now runs lower, and the row still has two keys.
Press ⌘Z once: both keys go back.
Compare with the setup's drag at three seconds, made with no row picked: that one wrote a new key at the playhead.
Right-click the Position row's name and open Easing: pick Ease out quint.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Is picking the row by its name an obvious enough way to say move the whole thing, or would you reach for something else first?
With Scale picked, a resize adds the same number of percent to every key. Is adding the right feel, or should it multiply every key instead?
With a row picked, typing a new X or Y in the tool bar still keys the playhead. Should typed values move the whole row too?
Does the row's Easing list, the same one a segment offers, read right when it changes every segment of the row at once?
rough: No mock covers this drag as a picture; it matches the row for it in the mock's interaction table.
Only a drag on the canvas moves the whole row. The tool bar's typed X, Y, W, H and A still key the playhead with a row picked.
A picked row whose value the drag does not change (Opacity, then a move) leaves that row alone and keys Position at the playhead as usual.
Scale shifts by adding percent, and no key goes below 1 percent.
